tests.procedure: Under strong white light, check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, conformance of colour and compliance with the visual specification.

details.bpSpecification: White or almost white, crystalline masses, supplied as pellets, sticks or slabs, deliquescent, readily absorbing carbon dioxide
details.uspSpecification: White, or practically white, fused masses, in small pellets, in flakes, or sticks, and in other forms. Is hard and brittle and shows a crystalline fracture. Exposed to the air, it rapidly absorbs carbon dioxide and moisture
details.reference: BP 2024 (SC IV K.) Characters Section in Monographs (Hygroscopicity and Solubility); USP 2024 Description and Relative Solubility; BP/USP 2024 Monograph for Sodium Hydroxide

tests.procedure: Weigh 100 mg of powdered sample in a stoppered tube. Add 0.1 mL of solvent, shake vigorously 1 min, hold at 25.0 +/- 0.5 C for 15 min (repeat shaking once if not dissolved). Dissolved = very soluble. If not, add another 0.9 mL (total 1 mL) and repeat = freely soluble; another 2 mL = soluble; another 7 mL = sparingly soluble; if still not, weigh 10 mg in a stoppered tube, 10 mL solvent = slightly soluble; 1 mg in 10 mL = very slightly soluble; else practically insoluble. Repeat with alcohol (BP: ethanol 96 per cent).

details.sample: 100 mg powdered sample in stoppered tube (10 mg and 1 mg for the lower classes)
steps: 1 mg in 10 mL: very slightly soluble
details.bpSpecification: Very soluble in water, freely soluble in ethanol (96 per cent)
details.uspSpecification: Freely soluble in water and in alcohol

tests.procedure: Dissolve 0.1 g in 10 mL of water. USP/combined STM adds: dilute 1 mL of the solution to 100 mL with water. Measure with a calibrated pH meter. Minimum 11.0.

details.dilutionCombinedStm: 1 mL of the solution diluted to 100 mL with water (Sodium Hydroxide-SM.txt:30 only)
details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix V L. Determination of pH Values; USP 2024 pH <791>; BP/USP 2024 Monograph for Sodium Hydroxide

tests.procedure: 2 mL of solution S. Add 2 mL of a 150 g/L potassium carbonate solution. Heat to boiling; no precipitate is formed. Add 4 mL of potassium pyroantimonate solution. Heat to boiling. Allow to cool in iced water and, if necessary, rub the inside of the test tube with a glass rod. A dense white precipitate is formed.

details.solutionS: Dissolve 5.0 g in 12 mL of water. Add 17 mL of hydrochloric acid R1, adjust to pH 7 with a 103 g/L hydrochloric acid solution and dilute to 50 mL with water
details.specification: A dense white precipitate is formed
details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix VI Qualitative Reactions and Tests; USP 2024 Identification Tests - General <191>, Sodium

tests.source: Sodium Hydroxide__Sodium Hydroxide-SM.txt:30 (BP-only file :30; solution S :26)

tests.procedure: Dissolve 1.0 g in 10 mL of water. Compare 10 mL of solution S with the same volume of water. The solution is clear and colorless.

details.sample: 1.0 g in 10 mL water; compare 10 mL of solution S with 10 mL of water
details.specification: The solution is clear and colorless
details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix IV A. Clarity of Solution and IV B. Colour of Solution

tests.source: Sodium Hydroxide__Sodium Hydroxide-SM BP.txt:31 (also Sodium Hydroxide-SM.txt:31)

tests.procedure: Carbonates, calculated as Na2CO3, are determined in the BP assay: 1 mL of 1 M hydrochloric acid used in the second part of the titration (after adding methyl orange) is equivalent to 0.1060 g of Na2CO3.

details.equivalence: 1 mL of 1 M hydrochloric acid in the 2nd part of the titration is equivalent to 0.1060 g (106.0 mg) of Na2CO3
details.analystEntersFinalValue: Decision 2026-11-04: was Titration in the transcription; now Measurement, the analyst enters the final value.

tests.procedure: Sample solution: dissolve 0.25 g in 5 mL of water, acidify with about 4 mL of nitric acid, dilute to 15 mL with water, pour into a test tube containing 1 mL of silver nitrate solution R2. Standard: 10 mL of chloride standard solution (5 ppm Cl) and 5 mL of water, add 1 mL of dilute nitric acid, pour as a single addition into a test tube containing 1 mL of silver nitrate solution R2. Examine laterally against a black background. After standing 5 min protected from light, any opalescence in the test solution is not more intense than in the standard.

details.standard: chloride standard solution (5 ppm Cl): immediately before use dilute with water to 100 times its volume a solution containing sodium chloride equivalent to 0.824 g NaCl in 1000.0 mL
details.silverNitrateSolutionR2: 1.7 g silver nitrate in water, to 100 mL

tests.source: Sodium Hydroxide__Sodium Hydroxide-SM BP.txt:33 (also Sodium Hydroxide-SM.txt:33; reagents :26)

tests.procedure: Sample solution: dissolve 0.75 g in 6 mL of distilled water, adjust to pH 7 with hydrochloric acid, dilute to 15 mL with distilled water. Add this solution to 2.5 mL of a mixture of 3 mL of 250 g/L barium chloride and 4.5 mL of sulfate standard solution (10 ppm SO4) R1. Shake, stand 1 min, add 0.5 mL of acetic acid. Standard: 15 mL of sulfate standard solution (10 ppm SO4) in place of the sample solution, same treatment. After 5 min any opalescence in the test solution is not more intense than in the standard.

details.standard: sulfate standard solution (10 ppm SO4) R1: immediately before use dilute with ethanol (30 per cent V/V) to 100 times its volume a solution containing dipotassium sulfate equivalent to 0.181 g K2SO4 in 100.0 mL ethanol (30 per cent V/V)

tests.source: Sodium Hydroxide__Sodium Hydroxide-SM BP.txt:34 (also Sodium Hydroxide-SM.txt:34; reagents :26)

tests.procedure: Sample: 10 mL of solution S. Add 2 mL of 200 g/L citric acid monohydrate solution and 0.1 mL of thioglycolic acid, mix, make alkaline with ammonia, dilute to 20 mL with water. Standard: 10 mL of iron standard solution (1 ppm Fe) treated the same way. After 5 min any pink colour in the test solution is not more intense than in the standard.

details.standard: iron standard solution (1 ppm Fe): dilute iron standard solution (20 ppm Fe) to 20 times its volume with water immediately before use; the 20 ppm solution: dilute with water to 10 times its volume a solution containing ferric ammonium sulfate equivalent to 0.863 g and 25 mL of dilute sulfuric acid in 500.0 mL

tests.source: Sodium Hydroxide__Sodium Hydroxide-SM BP.txt:35 (also Sodium Hydroxide-SM.txt:35; reagents :26)

tests.procedure: AAS (calibration curve from three standards). Diluent: 1% hydrochloric acid solution. Standard stock: 25.41 ug/mL sodium chloride in Diluent (contains 10 ug/mL sodium). Standards: 6.0, 7.5 and 9.0 mL of stock to separate 100 mL volumetric flasks, dilute with Diluent to volume = 0.6, 0.75, 0.9 ug/mL sodium. Sample stock: 1.303 mg/mL sodium hydroxide in Diluent. Sample solution: 0.1 mL of sample stock to a 100 mL flask, dilute with Diluent to volume. Blank: Diluent. Plot absorbance vs concentration (ug/mL) of sodium, correlation coefficient NLT 0.995. Percent sodium = (CS/CU) x 100.

details.technique: atomic absorption spectrophotometry (AAS, calibration curve; treat as ICP method per README rule 6)
details.standardStock: 25.41 ug/mL NaCl in Diluent = 10 ug/mL Na
details.standardPrep: 6.0, 7.5, 9.0 mL of stock each to 100 mL with Diluent
details.samplePrep: 0.1 mL of sample stock to 100 mL with Diluent
details.calculation: Result = (CS/CU) x 100; CS = Na concentration in sample solution from the curve (ug/mL); CU = NaOH concentration in the sample solution (ug/mL)
details.reference: USP 2024 Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy <852>; USP 2024 Monograph for Sodium Hydroxide

tests.heldBack: needs the held-back method "Sodium by AAS (sodium hydroxide USP)"

tests.procedure: AAS (calibration curve from three standards). Diluent: 1% hydrochloric acid solution. Standard stock: 1.907 mg/mL potassium chloride, previously dried at 105 C for 2 h, in water; 5.0 mL of this to a 1.0 L flask, dilute with Diluent to volume = 5 ug/mL potassium. Standards: 2.0, 5.0 and 10.0 mL of that solution to separate 100 mL flasks, dilute with Diluent = 0.10, 0.25, 0.50 ug/mL potassium. Sample stock: 0.5 mg/mL sodium hydroxide. Sample solution: 50 ug/mL sodium hydroxide in Diluent, prepared from the sample stock. Blank: Diluent. Correlation coefficient NLT 0.99. Result = (CS/CU) x 100.

details.technique: atomic absorption spectrophotometry (AAS, calibration curve; treat as ICP method per README rule 6)
details.standardStock: 1.907 mg/mL KCl (dried at 105 C for 2 h) in water; 5.0 mL to 1.0 L with Diluent = 5 ug/mL K
details.standardPrep: 2.0, 5.0, 10.0 mL of the 5 ug/mL K solution each to 100 mL with Diluent
details.samplePrep: 50 ug/mL NaOH in Diluent prepared from the sample stock
details.calculation: Result = (CS/CU) x 100; CS = K concentration in sample solution from the curve (ug/mL); CU = NaOH concentration in the sample solution (ug/mL)
details.reference: USP 2024 Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy <852>; USP 2024 Monograph for Sodium Hydroxide

tests.heldBack: needs the held-back method "Potassium by AAS (sodium hydroxide USP)"

tests.procedure: A solution (1 in 20) is complete, clear, and colorless to slightly colored.

details.sample: solution 1 in 20 (1 part in 20; solvent not stated)

tests.procedure: Dissolve 2.000 g in about 80 mL of carbon dioxide-free water. Add 0.3 mL of phenolphthalein solution. Titrate with 1 M hydrochloric acid. Add 0.3 mL of methyl orange solution. Continue the titration with 1 M hydrochloric acid. 1 mL of 1 M hydrochloric acid used in the 2nd part is equivalent to 0.1060 g of Na2CO3; 1 mL used in the combined titrations is equivalent to 40.00 mg of total alkali, calculated as NaOH.

details.dissolveIn: about 80 mL carbon dioxide-free water (water boiled a few minutes and protected from the atmosphere while cooling and storage)
details.titrant: 1 M hydrochloric acid VS (103.0 g HCl diluted to 1000.0 mL with water)
details.twoStageTitration: first stage with phenolphthalein; add methyl orange and continue (second part)
details.equivalence: 1 mL of 1 M HCl in combined titrations = 40.00 mg total alkali as NaOH; 1 mL of 1 M HCl in the 2nd part = 0.1060 g (106.0 mg) Na2CO3
details.standardizationOfTitrant: Dissolve 0.950 g trometamol in 50 mL water R. Titrate with the hydrochloric acid solution, end point with 0.1 mL methyl orange solution, yellowish-red colour (1 mL of 1 M HCl = 121.1 mg C4H11NO3)
details.calculation: %Assay = (E.p x Eq.wt x F / Wt) x 100; E.p = end point (mL), Eq.wt = 106.0 mg and 40.00 mg, F = factor of titrant, Wt = weight of sample (g)

tests.source: Sodium Hydroxide__Sodium Hydroxide-SM BP.txt:36 (also Sodium Hydroxide-SM.txt:39; titrant standardization :26)

tests.procedure: Sample 1.5 g; blank 40.0 mL carbon dioxide-free water. Direct titration, titrant 1 N sulfuric acid VS, visual end point. Dissolve the sample in 40 mL of carbon dioxide-free water, cool to room temperature, add phenolphthalein TS, titrate with 1 N sulfuric acid VS; at discharge of the pink colour record the volume (VS1). Add methyl orange TS, continue to a persistent pink colour, record the volume (VS2). Perform a blank determination and correct. Total alkali (as NaOH) % = {[(VS2 - VB) x N x F1]/W} x 100, F1 = 40.00 mg/mEq. Sodium carbonate % = {[(VS2 - VS1) x N x F2]/W} x 100, F2 = 106.0 mg/mEq. W is sample weight in mg.

details.titrant: 1 N sulfuric acid VS (27 mL sulfuric acid added slowly with stirring to water to make 1000 mL)
indicators: phenolphthalein TS (1 g in 100 mL alcohol)
methyl orange TS (100 mg in 100 mL water, filter if necessary)

endPoints.VS1: discharge of the pink colour of phenolphthalein
endPoints.VS2: persistent pink colour with methyl orange

details.standardizationOfTitrant: Accurately weigh about 5.0 g tromethamine (dried per label or, if not available, at 105 C for 3 h). Dissolve in 50 mL water, add 2 drops bromocresol green TS (50 mg in 100 mL alcohol). Titrate with 1 N sulfuric acid to a pale-yellow end point. Each 121.14 mg tromethamine = 1 mL of 1 N sulfuric acid. N = mg tromethamine / (121.14 x mL H2SO4)

calculations.totalAlkaliPercent: {[(VS2 - VB) x N x F1]/W} x 100; VB = blank volume, N = actual normality, W = sample weight in mg
calculations.sodiumCarbonatePercent: {[(VS2 - VS1) x N x F2]/W} x 100

details.specification: 95.0%-100.5% of total alkali; NMT 3.0% of sodium carbonate (Na2CO3)
details.reference: USP 2024 Titrimetry <541>; USP 2024 Monograph for Sodium Hydroxide

tests.procedure: Sodium carbonate is obtained from the same USP total alkali titration: % Na2CO3 = {[(VS2 - VS1) x N x 106.0]/W} x 100.

details.analystEntersFinalValue: Decision 2026-11-04: was Titration in the transcription; now Measurement, the analyst enters the final value.

openQuestions.question: Retest minimum sample quantity conflicts: Sodium Hydroxide-SM.txt:42 says routine and retention 50 g, periodic retesting 100 g; Sodium Hydroxide-SM BP.txt:38 says routine and retention 30 g, retesting 60 g; the 2023 STM (no code) says testing 30 gm, retention 60 gm (:47); both spec sheets say 50 gm. Routine = 50 g recorded from the spec sheets; retest left null.
openQuestions.source: Sodium Hydroxide__Sodium Hydroxide-SM.txt:42; Sodium Hydroxide__Sodium Hydroxide-SM BP.txt:38; Sodium Hydroxide__Specifications sheet Sodium Hydroxide BP.txt:21

openQuestions.question: Identification pH procedure differs between the two method files: the combined STM dilutes 1 mL of the 0.1 g/10 mL solution to 100 mL before measuring, the BP-only STM measures the undiluted solution. Both recorded in the test details; confirm which is correct for BP.
openQuestions.source: Sodium Hydroxide__Sodium Hydroxide-SM.txt:30; Sodium Hydroxide__Sodium Hydroxide-SM BP.txt:30

openQuestions.question: BP assay calculation %Assay = E.p x Eq.wt x F / Wt x 100 defines Wt in grams but Eq.wt in mg (40.00 or 106.0 mg), which gives 10x too large a result unless Wt is in mg; it also does not say which Eq.wt applies to the carbonate figure. Formula recorded as written.

The BP assay does not state how the first (phenolphthalein) and second (methyl orange) titration volumes combine for total alkali versus carbonates (volumes V1/V2 not named, unlike the USP assay). The carbonate figure (max 2.0 per cent) is only referenced to 'the assay'.

Potassium AAS calculation text says 'Calculate the percentage of sodium' although the test is for potassium; the sample stock solvent (0.5 mg/mL sodium hydroxide) is not stated. Recorded as potassium and solvent unstated.

Appearance of solution: sample is 'Dissolve 1.0 g in 10 mL of water' but it is then compared 'Compare 10 mL of Solution S with the same volume of water'; Solution S is 5.0 g in 12 mL/17 mL HCl R1 diluted to 50 mL, not the 1.0 g solution. Which solution is examined is unclear.
openQuestions.source: Sodium Hydroxide__Sodium Hydroxide-SM BP.txt:31; Sodium Hydroxide__Sodium Hydroxide-SM.txt:31

openQuestions.question: Insoluble Substances and Organic Matter: 'A solution (1 in 20)' has no stated solvent or amount; recorded as stated.

Header of the Tests section says physical tests are done on each received container and chemical tests on a mixed sample. Description is explicitly per container (flagged); whether Solubility is also a per-container physical test is not stated.

Which STM file is the issued one: 'Sodium Hydroxide- STM.txt' (no STM number, BP/USP 2023 references, 2023 wording) is superseded in content by the coded STM-RM-150 v1/0 files (10-07-2024) used here. Confirm.
